Soojin / Team / Anthony —

Short recommendation (for procurement): Choose a mixed-reserve approach centered on A100-80GB as the primary reserved SKU with a small L4 pool for cheap embedding throughput and an H100 burst lane for latency-sensitive long-context generation spikes. Rationale: A100-80GB offers the best balance of memory headroom (useful for 64k contexts and larger KV caches) and steady per-token throughput at reserve economics. L4 is highly cost-efficient for dense embedding traffic and small-sequence inference; use it for the 30% embedding workload and for precomputing caches. H100 should be reserved in a small burst pool (or as on-demand fallback) where extremely low p50/p95 latency is mandatory for the highest-tier endpoints.

Operations caveats / sizing rules of thumb:
- Memory headroom: provision A100 for nodes that will host long-context or RLHF workloads — prefer 80GB variant if you plan to hold large KV caches and run multi-job mixing.
- Throughput vs. cost: put bulk steady-state gen and RLHF batch work on A100; L4 for high QPS, low-cost embedding endpoints to reduce token cost. H100 is ideal when you need single-thread latency at scale but is costly as a reserve.
- Burst strategy: configure automated routing policies that route to A100 reserved first, failover to L4 for embeddings, and route to H100 only for premium routes or if latency SLOs are at risk.
- Quantization: if model ops can accept int8/4 quantized weights, L4 becomes even more attractive for embeddings.

I'll drop a quick sizing sketch after lunch with slot counts based on their 6M token estimate.

—Karthik

Karthik nailed the tradeoffs. Adding ops-level notes for the SOW and procurement: 

1) Capacity phasing: Start with an A100-focused reserve sized for ~70% of predictable gen and RLHF batch traffic. Add an L4 pool sized to absorb 100% of embedding QPS at baseline (these nodes are cheap and reduce token egress costs). Keep H100 as an hourly-burst slot pool (or short-term reserved burst) sized for 10–15% of peak gen traffic.
2) Autoscaling rules: prefer vertical slotting within A100 fleet for long-context sessions (preserve KV), and horizontal scale for L4 embedding workers.
3) Cache sizing: allocate 20–30% of A100 memory budget to KV/prefix caches when serving 64k contexts to avoid repeated recompute costs.
4) SLAs & fallbacks: contract should specify that H100 burst capacity is best-effort placement and that guaranteed p50/p95 SLAs apply only to the primary reserved SKU (A100).

I'll assemble a short bullet appendix for the SOW we can attach to procurement.

—Ben
